record.title: Khorgos cross-border cooperation-centre visitor suspension during COVID-19
record.start_precision: Closed by 27 January 2020; exact COVID-related onset and earliest bound remain unknown.
record.end_precision: See phase-specific observed or permission endpoint
record.scope: The enclosed bilateral International Centre for Border Cooperation, not the whole frontier
record.crossings: Khorgos International Centre for Border Cooperation
record.direction: Visitor access across the centre boundary; first observed return is Kazakhstan to the Chinese section
record.movement: Visitors to the cross-border tourism and shopping centre
record.exceptions: Ordinary road/rail freight and commercial-cargo clearance follow separate rules; the first observed visitor cohort does not prove every access category resumed.
record.imposing_authority: Chinese and Kazakh cooperation-centre and border authorities
record.enforcement: See the separate operational observations and formal permissions in the linked phases.
record.record_type: Facility-specific intentional restriction with traffic-scoped phases
record.relationship: No centre-specific parent found in the baseline or upstream R01–R08 packets. CC002 is a national Kazakhstan entry/exit policy, not this facility-specific visitor interruption.
record.status_observation: Historical evidence only; no current border openness or closure inferred.
record.policy_group: COVID-19 land-facility controls; traffic-specific phases retained
record.current_timing: dated evidence; numeric duration withheld; see qualification
record.current_corrections: The centre was already reported closed for coronavirus prevention by 27 January 2020; this is a latest-onset bound, not an exact observed start. The report distinguishes an earlier holiday closure from 22 January, whose onset is not imported into this COVID phase. The earliest COVID-related onset and uninterrupted continuity are not established, so numeric duration remains withheld. Kazakh visitors were observed entering the Chinese section on 17 April 2023. The abandoned 8 January plan and the separate 24 April normal-operations announcement are not substituted for that scoped observed return. Ordinary road freight, rail traffic and commercial import permissions are outside this phase.
record.rationale_coding_status: Source-attributed coding accepted after separate challenge; qualifications retained
record.rationale_phase_note: Human disease control applies to the initiating restriction. Later reopening procedures are not new inferred motives; overlapping phases are not added.

Start earliest remains null; the earlier 22 January holiday shutdown is not adopted as the COVID onset. Keep withheld_unknown_onset, null numeric duration, complete/exact=0 and the observed 17 April 2023 endpoint. The abandoned 8 January and separate 24 April plans remain distinct. Health and biosecurity / Human disease control is supported by the regional administration and direct sanitary-doctor statements. The earlier holiday context is retained as a qualification, not recoded as the initiating rationale of this COVID phase. The actual-return article and April announcement were freshly read. One failed old link and one focused search led to four contemporary full-text reports, preserved with receipts. Astana Times/Zakon share an administration origin; the tour site is commercial and its plan is not authenticated official publication. Cached failed-plan and scope accounts remain labelled reuse. The phase stays unlocated at the cooperation centre, with the Kazakhstan-to-China visitor direction and evidence-only temporal rule. Source linkage is synchronized; no national or nearby freight geometry is inherited.
